title: Cap. VI Arg. 4 close: special vocation of mercy — election ad fidem, not ex fide
pass_a_gloss: I reduce this reason into a sum. There is a certain special vocation of mercy, which is administered to certain men, not because they were considered as faithful, but because they were predestined that they might become faithful. This vocation flowed from an antecedent will infallibly destining such ones to eternal life. Not of all is such a vocation, but only of the elect. Therefore election depends from the good pleasure of God, not from the act of men. Therefore it is unto faith, not from faith. For by this vocation the will of every predestined person is excited that he may believe efficaciously, even if he is so averse and fierce that he persecutes believers, Augustine, Against Two Letters of the Pelagians, book 1, chapter 19.
pass_b_english: Sum: there is a special vocation of mercy given to some — not because they were already counted faithful, but because they were predestined to become faithful. It flows from an antecedent will that infallibly destines them to eternal life. Not everyone has that vocation — only the elect. So election hangs on God's good pleasure, not on human act. So it is unto faith, not from faith. By this calling every predestined will is stirred to believe efficaciously — even if so hostile and fierce that he persecutes believers (Augustine, Against Two Letters of the Pelagians 1.19).
source_text: In summam redigo hanc rationem. Est quaedam vocatio specialis misericordiae, quae administratur hominibus quibusdam, non quia fuerunt considerati ut fideles, sed quia praedestinati ut fierent fideles. Haec vocatio fluxit ab antecedanea voluntate tales ad vitam aeternam infallibiliter destinante. Non omnium talis est vocatio, sed tantum electorum. Ergo electio ex beneplacito Dei non ex actu hominum dependet. Ergo est ad fidem, non ex fide. Nam hac vocatione voluntas cujusliber praedestinati, ut credat efficaciter, excitatur, etiam si tam sit aversus et ferox ut credentes persequatur, August. Contra 2. Epist. Pelag. lib. 1. cap. 19.
